quotes.text: If tagging a file takes 30 seconds, and the user doesn't personally benefit from the metadata, they will skip it. And if skipping is faster than doing it, skipping becomes the default behavior.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in plain terms why manual tagging fails regardless of training.

quotes.text: Manual tagging asks the user to declare what a file is. Graph-based governance observes what the file actually is in the context of the organization.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp contrast between declared and context-derived metadata.

quotes.text: Real governance happens before the file settles into storage, not after. The difference isn't technical. It is structural, and it determines whether your metadata is a foundation or a repair job.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Argues for governance at the point of creation instead of scheduled cleanup.

quotes.text: When an AI agent can query every document in your tenant, the quality of your metadata determines the quality of its answers. Bad metadata means bad answers, missing metadata means missing answers.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links metadata quality directly to AI answer quality.

quotes.text: Manual tagging was never a governance strategy. It was a hope that users would do unpaid work with no visible payoff
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable verdict that summarizes the episode's thesis.

takeaways: Manual dropdown tagging cannot scale with hybrid work and content volume, so untagged files become dark data that search, compliance tools and AI agents cannot use.
Event-driven middleware on Azure Functions can query Microsoft Graph for context, write schema extension properties and apply Purview sensitivity labels at the moment content is created.
Roll out in phases (audit, a small taxonomy, a single-team pilot, scale, optimize) and keep humans in the loop for low-confidence and high-risk classifications.
hook: If your Microsoft 365 governance still depends on users picking values from dropdowns, most of your content is probably untagged and invisible. This episode is for governance, compliance and SharePoint architects, and shows how Graph-driven middleware can classify and label content automatically so search, DLP and Copilot work on reliable metadata.
